issues: Source 3 cited Wikipedia ('Semayne's case' infobox, 'Michaelmas Term, 1604') for the displayDate term. Wikipedia's own reference for the case is Sheppard's Liberty Fund edition of Coke's writings; it is replaced with that edition's case heading, '(1604) Michaelmas Term, 2 James 1 In the Court of King's Bench', read in the Online Library of Liberty's PDF (--check FOUND).

sourceFixes.institution: Liberty Fund, Online Library of Liberty: The Selected Writings and Speeches of Sir Edward Coke, vol. 1, ed. Steve Sheppard
sourceFixes.title: Semayne's Case, (1604) Michaelmas Term, 2 James 1, King's Bench (5 Co. Rep. 91a)
sourceFixes.quote: Semayne’s Case. (1604) Michaelmas Term, 2 James 1 In the Court of King’s Bench. First Published in the Reports, volume 5, page 91a.
sourceFixes.note: Replaces a Wikipedia citation (Semayne's case). The Online Library of Liberty's PDF of the printed edition (© 2003 Liberty Fund); --check FOUND on 2026-09-23. The editor's heading dates the case to Michaelmas Term of 2 James I (1604), in the King's Bench. The report then opens 'In an Action on the Case by Peter Semayne, Plaintiff, and Richard Gresham, Defendant' (--check FOUND), which gives the full case name. The 1826 edition of Coke's Reports, vol. 3 (archive.org item reportssiredwar00cokegoog), heads the case 'Mich. 2. Jac. 1. In the King's Bench'. That was read in OCR text, so it could not be checked with --check.

issues: Source 4 cited Wikipedia ('Great Flood of 1862') to corroborate the San Francisco sitting. Wikipedia's reference is a San Joaquin County Historical Society article, whose PDF now returns 404. It is replaced with the California State Capitol Museum's history page, which says the flood-bound Legislature completed its 1862 session in San Francisco's Merchants Exchange Building from 24 January to 15 May 1862 (--check FOUND). This agrees with Concurrent Resolution No. XI (source 3) and puts the 18 April 1862 approval inside the San Francisco sitting.

sourceFixes.institution: California State Capitol Museum (State of California)
sourceFixes.title: Construction — History of the Capitol
sourceFixes.quote: They briefly adjourned before completing the session in San Francisco’s Merchants Exchange Building from January 24 th until May 15 th , 1862.
sourceFixes.note: Replaces a Wikipedia citation (Great Flood of 1862). --check FOUND on 2026-09-23; the spaces in '24 th' and '15 th ,' are how the page's superscript ordinals extract. The same page says 'On January 6 th , 1862, the Legislature convened in the midst of the deluge. The fourth in a series of floods inundated the city on January 11 th , and the Senate passed a resolution to adjourn to San Francisco for the remainder of the session.' (--check FOUND). Undated page; 'date' is the access year. The 'Merchants Exchange Building' matches the 'Exchange Building' on Battery Street named in Concurrent Resolution No. XI.
